judge2.comment: Accurate, well-evidenced report matching D-01, D-02 (rated P3, below the key's P2) and D-05, with two supported extras: the 5,000원 즉시 할인 that has no stated source and is reconciled only at the page end, and the order-complete screen with no controls. It saw the light-grey installment note in its persona notes but never reported it (D-03), and the Toss Pay visibility finding is not D-04.

findings.title: No visible response for about 2.6 s after tapping the pay button

Destructive '전체삭제' button sits directly beside the primary pay button in the sticky bar
Pay button total differs from the visible item prices, and the reason is only below the fold

I estimated positions from the downscaled CSS screenshot. Statements about size and visibility are qualitative, not measured.

judge1.comment: The most accurate and best-calibrated report: D-01, D-02 and D-05 are all rated P2 and backed by driver data and snapshot IDs, plus the same two valid extras (unexplained price difference, dead-end done screen). Like E, it saw the faint installment text in its notes but did not report D-03, and it framed the grid as looking too short rather than as 12 undifferentiated options (D-04).

judge2.comment: Strong and precise: D-01, D-02 and D-05 are cited to driver fields and snapshot ids, plus the same two valid extras as Arm B (discount with no stated source; completion overlay with no next action), with no false positives. It noticed the faint installment note only in its persona notes (D-03 missed); the grid 'false floor' finding is accurate but does not identify choice overload (D-04).

Time slot coordinate click provides no visual feedback

Did not realize first time slot click (coordinate-based) hadn't produced visual feedback until examining subsequent screenshots - required second click with different targeting method to confirm

judge2.comment: Both findings come from the agent's own targeting problems: a text= selector miss, and 'no visual feedback' taps that actually hit the disabled 11:00 and 16:00 slots rather than 15:30. No real defect is reported, and a persona note says 수 30 was selected when 화 29 was.

judge2.comment: Clearly caught the top-only error. The pale submit button is merged with a required-marker complaint, and the toast finding is framed as 'dark/text-heavy' and says only that it 'may disappear', without verifying it. It missed the color-only slots, and every persona note is a 'see next' placeholder, which weakens traceability.

judge2.comment: Found all four defects that apply without a profile (color-only slots, top-only error, disappearing pending-notice toast, pale submit), plus two real extras (stale error box, dead-end completion screen), with no false positives. The P1 headline says the toast vanishes 'after about 5 seconds', but the run only showed it was gone by the 5 s check; the driver measured 1.5 s, so the headline understates the issue.

findings.title: Phone-number error shown only as a top banner, not at the field

judge1.comment: Every finding is accurate. It misses the pending-status toast, the colour-only slots and the pale submit button, all of which were on screen, and its evidence fields are bare snapshot IDs. The required-marker and summary-bar findings are low-value and left uncounted.

judge2.comment: Accurate and clearly evidenced, but it matched only D-15. It missed the pending-notice toast even though it saw it, and also missed the color-only slots and the pale submit button. The stale-error and dead-end extras are real; the wording, required-marker and summary-bar findings are nitpicks.

findings.title: The 'received, confirmation by KakaoTalk within 30 minutes' message is only in a disappearing toast
Phone-number error is shown only in a top banner, not on the field, and stays after the field is filled
Error banner insertion pushes the whole form down

Submit button looks pale or disabled in every state, although it is active

judge1.comment: An accurate, well-evidenced report: it catches the toast (it saw the toast disappear), the error shown only at the top and the pale submit button, and it frames claims as hypotheses with honest limitations, including correctly declining to flag the checkbox decoy. It misses the colour-only slots, and its layout-shift and required-marker findings are plausible but low-value, so they are not counted as extras.

judge2.comment: Careful, well-hedged report. It caught the top-only error, the disappearing pending notice (confirmed with a fresh snapshot) and the pale submit button, and explicitly declined to report the checkbox-size decoy. It missed the color-only slot encoding; its pixel figures match driver geometry, and its separate layout-shift and required-marker findings add little.

findings.title: The only message saying the booking still needs store confirmation disappears within about 5 s, and what stays reads like a finished booking
The missing-phone error appears only at the top of the page, far from the submit button, and nothing marks the phone field
Open and closed time slots differ only by red vs green color

agent_limitations: The emulated screenshots showed no on-screen keyboard, and text went in through the driver's type action. So I could not check the keyboard type for the phone field, whether the keyboard hides the top error box or the submit button, or any auto-formatting.

I left the phone number blank on purpose, as the scenario required, and I read each full screenshot after every action. That made me more likely to notice the top error box than a real user whose eyes stay near the bottom button, so my noticing it does not show that real users would.
I only looked at the toast twice: right after submitting, and after a 5000 ms wait. I know it was gone within about 5 s, but not exactly how long it stayed.

I did not tap a closed (red) slot, try other dates, or press browser back from the completion screen. judge1.comment: Found 4 of the 5 key defects (the vanishing pending-status toast, the error shown only at the top, time slots told apart only by colour, the pale submit button). Every claim matches the screenshots, including the driver's element boxes (the form shifts about 75 px, focus stays on the submit button). It also adds two real extras: the completion screen is a dead end, and the error says to enter the number 'correctly' when the field was empty and stays after the fix. It missed only the profile-dependent reach problem with the '다음' button, and it rated the submit contrast issue P3, framing it as 'looks disabled'.

judge2.comment: Best report: all four applicable defects with accurate evidence (toast gone within 5 s, a 74 px form shift that matches the driver's element boxes, focus not moved) and hypotheses labeled as such. The dead-end completion screen and the stale, imprecise phone error are sound extras.

findings.title: Success screen lacks visible exit affordance

judge1.comment: A confused 18-step run that kept trying a second 2,000,000원 transfer through elements hidden behind the success overlay. The dead-end finding is valid but cites snapshots 005 and 006 (confirmation sheet and spinner) as success frames, and the text-selector failure is a driver issue, not a UX problem.

protocol_violations: Acted on elements that were not visible: after the full-screen success overlay appeared, it followed DOM element analysis instead of the screenshot. It typed 2000000 into the covered amount field and tapped the hidden 다음 and ‹ controls (steps 10-17; target_hit false on steps 14 and 16).
judge2.comment: Only the dead-end finding is valid, and even that one cites snapshots 005-006, which show the confirmation sheet and the sending spinner. The 'text selector fails on placeholder' finding is a Playwright tooling artifact, not a UX problem (the input has aria-label 보낼 금액). 12 of the 18 steps were wasted on hidden controls.

I judged the chip add-versus-replace behavior from one tap only, not from repeated taps.

judge2.comment: The chip finding matches D-07 (small, tightly spaced chips with mis-tap risk), but its title wrongly says the chips replace the amount; the page code adds. The dead-end success screen and the missing daily-limit info are valid extras (the clean variant adds a '1일 이체 한도' hint). The P2 김서연 finding is about what the #confirm-account line says, not D-08's 12 px legibility, so it matches nothing.

findings.title: Success screen has no exit, confirm or next-step control
Daily transfer limit is not shown before sending

A larger amount (for example, one near the 2,350,000원 withdrawable balance) might have triggered the limit notice.

judge1.comment: Two accurate, concise findings (the completion dead end, and the daily limit not shown, which the clean variant fixes) with honest limitations. It identified no seeded defect, even though D-06, D-07 and D-08 were on screen during the run.

judge2.comment: Both findings are accurate and well-evidenced: the success screen has no exit, and the daily limit is not shown before sending. No planted defect was found, and the limit branch (D-09) never triggered because 1,000,000원 is exactly at the limit.

findings.title: Success screen has no way to leave it
No daily transfer limit information anywhere in the flow
Confirmation sheet's primary/secondary buttons sit flush against the bottom screen edge

The reach finding is wrong, though: the snapshot puts 취소/보내기 16 px above the viewport bottom (sheet padding, not flush), and a bottom placement is the recommended thumb zone; no seeded defect was identified.

judge2.comment: The dead-end and missing-limit findings are valid. The reach finding is wrong: 취소/보내기 are not flush with the bottom edge (the sheet has 16 px bottom padding), and bottom placement is the recommended thumb zone. No planted defect was found.

findings.title: Transfer-complete page has no button, header or receipt details
Unexplained name 김서연 in the send confirmation
Success check mark renders as a dotted line
Quick-amount buttons look short and tightly packed

agent_limitations: The goal did not state a starting amount. I chose 1,000,000 won with +100만 to try to reach the limit path. The app accepted it and no daily limit notice appeared, so I never saw the limit notice, its wording or placement, or the reduce-to-50,000 resend. This run says nothing about that path, and I stopped because the transfer to 홍길동 had gone through.

I judged the dotted check mark and the button heights by eye from CSS-scale screenshots only. I measured no sizes and cannot separate a page defect from a screenshot scaling artifact for the check mark.
I cannot tell whether the missing button on the success page is a deliberate end state of this demo or a real gap. The driver offered no back action and I did not try one.

I am an automated operator reading screenshots, so reach, one-handed and thumb-comfort statements are hypotheses. I did not test typing an amount with the keyboard, tapping 다음 with no recipient or amount, the ‹ back arrow, or the 취소 button.

judge1.comment: The only clean hit on D-07 (short, tightly packed chips, +10만/+100만 next to each other, taps correctly described as adding, no invented sizes), plus a well-evidenced completion dead end and honest limitations. The dotted check is a font-fallback artifact of the test container (hedged false positive), and the 김서연 item points at the D-08 element but misreads the user's own passbook-display name instead of flagging the 12 px text, so it was not credited; like every arm it sent exactly 1,000,000원, so D-09 was never reached.

judge2.comment: The clearest D-07 match: +10만 and +100만 are neighbours, a mis-tap gives a tenfold error, and it correctly notes that taps add. The dead-end finding is a valid extra. The 'dotted check' is a glyph-rendering artifact of the test environment (the check is a text ✓ and stays pixelated even in the full-resolution PNG), so it counts as a false positive; the 김서연 finding is about content, not D-08 legibility.

findings.title: Transfer completion screen is a dead end: no confirm, close, home or back control
Daily transfer limit and remaining limit are not shown anywhere before sending

agent_limitations: The goal did not give a starting amount. I chose 1,000,000원 with the '+100만' chip, and it went through with no daily-limit notice. So the recovery path this goal was about (limit notice, reduce to 50,000원, send again) never ran. Any problems in that flow (notice wording, how the amount gets edited, the retry control) are untested in this run. I did not make a second transfer to force the notice, because the transfer to 홍길동 was already done and a second one would not match the persona's intent.
